sources.title: Water and wastewater capacity
sources.verified_claim: A site-specific pre-planning enquiry can confirm network capacity and identify actions if capacity is unavailable; generic network coverage is not a candidate capacity result.

sources.title: Working near our pipes
sources.verified_claim: Significant works near mains or sewers require asset-location review and may require diversion or build-over controls; exact pipe proximity is essential.

sources.title: Adopting sewers and other assets
sources.verified_claim: Section 104 adoption requires compliant design, legal agreement, inspection and vesting; constructing a sewer does not mean it has already been adopted.

sources.title: Diverting or closing a public sewer
sources.verified_claim: Section 185 diversion requests undergo technical review, agreements and inspection; a public sewer on land does not imply a diversion is approved.

sources.title: Connecting to a sewer
sources.verified_claim: Direct public-sewer connections require permission, plans and inspection; connection status depends on exact sewer ownership, point and approved works.

sources.title: Requisitioning a new public sewer or lateral drain
sources.verified_claim: A sewer requisition is a developer-funded route where connection cannot otherwise be delivered, often because of third-party land; it is not automatic service availability.

sources.title: Trade effluent
sources.verified_claim: Trade effluent, including some construction discharges, requires consent with conditions and limits; candidate discharge need cannot be inferred without activity facts.

sources.title: Developers
sources.verified_claim: Ofwat describes developer connections, requisitioning, self-lay and NAV mechanisms; regulatory market routes are not evidence of a completed site connection.
